gen_risks.description: Security instability and armed conflict in FCV zones impeding project access, service delivery, and physical monitoring.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare, consult upon, disclose, and implement country-specific Security Risk Assessments (SRAs) and Security Management Plans (SMPs) in FCV areas.
gen_risks.evidence: Political instability, particularly in the North-West and South-West regions, may disrupt service delivery

gen_risks.description: Inadequate financial management controls leading to questionable expenditures or documentation gaps in remote/decentralized project activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adapt standard financial management manuals for local partners, customize accounting software within three months, and deploy internal/external auditors.
gen_risks.evidence: several activities under the project like workshops, trainings and the local-level capacity building are at risk to generate questionable expenditures

gen_risks.description: Macro-fiscal pressures, low domestic budget allocations, and declining oil revenues threatening long-term financial sustainability of health security investments.
gen_risks.mitigation: Assist governments in integrating health security into Medium-Term Expenditure Frameworks, tracking budgets, and exploring domestic resource mobilization and PPP models.
gen_risks.evidence: The country’s macroeconomic stability has been impacted by declining oil revenues and structural economic challenges... domestic funding for health per capita was just US$10.79

gen_risks.description: Procurement delays, governance bottlenecks, weak contract management, and limited supplier competition in fragile/FCV market settings.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit qualified procurement specialists, utilize STEP real-time tracking, adopt flexible procurement in FCV areas, and conduct early market engagement.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement Risks include delays, governance issues, weak contract management, and limited market competition in fragile settings.

gen_risks.description: Delays in project startup due to delayed PIU staffing, accounting software customization, POM adoption, or execution of inter-agency MoUs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Monitor compliance with legal covenants, establish PCIU/PIUs prior to or upon effectiveness, and utilize technical assistance for rapid onboarding.
gen_risks.evidence: The Recipient shall, not later than one (1) month after the Effective Date, appoint, assign, or recruit an accountant... environmental specialist

gen_risks.description: Exclusion of vulnerable or disadvantaged groups (e.g., IDPs, refugees, rural women) and inadequate stakeholder engagement in project activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement country-adapted Stakeholder Engagement Plans (SEPs), deploy citizen engagement feedback channels, and maintain accessible Grievance Redress Mechanisms.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential social risks are substantial and relate to: (i) inadequate stakeholder engagement... (ii) the exclusion of vulnerable or disadvantaged groups

gen_risks.description: Risks of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH) linked to labor influx and frontline healthcare worker deployment in communities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop country-specific SEA/SH Action Plans within two months, recruit dedicated GBV specialists, enforce codes of conduct, and establish GBV-sensitive GRMs.
gen_risks.evidence: The overall project SEA/SH risks are judged to be substantial... lack of institutional codes of conduct for health service providers

gen_risks.description: Environmental contamination and community health hazards resulting from improper management, handling, and disposal of hazardous healthcare and laboratory waste.
gen_risks.mitigation: Update and implement Biomedical Waste Management Plans (BMWMP), enforce biosafety/biosecurity guidelines, and apply site-specific ESMPs.
gen_risks.evidence: laboratories will be supplied with reagents, chemicals, and equipment that may constitute medical waste once used, all of which could pose community health risks

gen_risks.description: Climate change impacts (floods, extreme heat waves) damaging health infrastructure and triggering vector- and water-borne disease outbreaks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate climate resilience and EDGE level 1 energy efficiency standards in health facility refurbishments, and link climate alerts with health surveillance.
gen_risks.evidence: Climate change contributed to at least 50 percent of natural disasters registered in Cameroon, CAR, Chad, and RoC since they were mostly constituted of floods

gen_risks.description: Weak institutional capacity and coordination bottlenecks across multi-sectoral line ministries (health, livestock/veterinary, environment) under One Health.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish and operationalize National Steering Committees, multisectoral One Health platforms, and sign collaborative agreements (e.g., CEMAC-WOAH MoU).
gen_risks.evidence: gaps are primarily due to limited domestic and regional resources, weak institutional capacities and governance mechanisms, and insufficient multisectoral coordination

gen_risks.description: Administrative and political governance inefficiencies causing delays in adopting regionally harmonized health regulations, sample transport policies, and data sharing protocols.
gen_risks.mitigation: Leverage CEMAC's political mandate and direct communication lines with decision-makers to advocate and draft sub-regional conventions, supported by Regional Coordination Committee coordination.
gen_risks.evidence: Political and administrative inefficiencies could slow project execution.

gen_risks.description: Gender disparity and underrepresentation of female health workers in specialized field epidemiology (FETP) and veterinary epidemiology training.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct targeted female outreach, implement flexible training formats, establish minimum 30 percent gender targets for cohorts, and track gender gaps.
gen_risks.evidence: women dominate low-paid frontline roles but are largely absent from technical positions... partly due to limited access to training programs

gen_risks.description: Gaps in laboratory biosafety, biosecurity, and diagnostic quality management systems leading to testing delays or biohazard risks during pathogen handling.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement WHO SLIPTA quality improvement processes, establish regional laboratory protocols, upgrade lab infrastructure, and conduct biosafety/biosecurity training.
gen_risks.evidence: region commonly faces significant gaps in laboratory diagnostic capabilities, disease surveillance and information systems

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk (Moderate), considering fragility, socio-political instability, violence and weak governance of beneficiary countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close engagement by the World Bank to coordinate activities with other key partners.

gt_risks.description: Technical design risk (Substantial), considering the complexities of coordinating national-level and regional-level activities to align and build on each other, and the different levels of readiness at country-level.
gt_risks.mitigation: Exploring the possibility of a coordinated implementation arrangement with CEMAC as the lead technical coordination body for regional activities.

gt_risks.description: Weak institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability (Substantial), combined with overstretched or nonexistent PIUs in respective countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Strengthening the existing PIUs and intensive capacity building and targeted TA for newly established PIUs.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk (Substantial) due to weak governance structures and inadequate FM systems.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on fiduciary processes.

gt_risks.description: E&S risk (Substantial) given the security risks associated with service delivery in FCV (fragility, conflict, and violence) settings.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on managing E&S risks.
